sheet-48.description: Additional sheet of April 1919 covering the upper part of Cliffside Park on the Palisades, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. Anderson Avenue runs across the top and Edgewater Road down the middle; River View Avenue bounds the sheet on the east, and Cecila Avenue and Overlook Avenue the southwest. Between Anderson and Commercial Avenues are small residential blocks along Clark Terrace, Fulton Terrace and Millfred Terrace with a few brick-veneered and frame dwellings; east of Edgewater Road the blocks along Kearny, Hillside and Green Mount Avenues are platted but almost empty. A street railway right of way runs beside Commercial Avenue and crosses a steel bridge near the northeast corner. Long blocks of narrow lots line Palisades Avenue, Gorge Road and Summit Terrace on the diagonal; on Palisades Avenue stand a public garage with an underground gasoline tank, the Whitley Exerciser Company works and a real estate office. Cliffside Park High School, of brick with a gymnasium in the basement, occupies a large lot east of Edgewater Road. The south half has scattered dwellings, several stuccoed or of stone, along Adolphus Avenue, Cortland Place, Brandon Place, Long View and Winterburn Grove, and two streets east of Edgewater Road are lettered 'Not Named'. Much of the ground east of Edgewater Road is shown as vacant lots. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along most streets, and the margins refer to sheets 23, 30, 32, 35 and 36.
notes: Renamed since: Hillside Av is now Lindberg Avenue; Millfred Terrace is Willfred Terrace; Kearny Av is Kearney Avenue; Green Mount Av is Greenmount Avenue; Palisades Av is Palisade Avenue; River View Av is Riverview Avenue; Cecila Av is Cecelia Avenue; On Crest Pl is Oncrest Terrace; Long View is Longview Place.
The two streets lettered 'Not Named' east of Edgewater Road are now Williams Terrace (north) and Everett Place (south).
The upper Adolphus Av, east of Cecila Av, is now part of Cecelia Avenue.
A street railway right of way runs along the south side of Commercial Avenue, with a steel bridge at the northeast.
Cliffside Park High School stands east of Edgewater Road.
Cortland Place was left out of the control: all its modern junctions sit 3 to 4 m off the drawn line.
Sheet header reads 'Palisades, N.J.' and 'Add'l Sheet Apr. 1919'.

sheet-78-1.description: Main part of an additional sheet of April 1919 showing the southern part of Leonia, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 29 degrees so that north points to the upper left. Broad Avenue, 80 ft wide, runs down the west edge; Glenwood Avenue runs parallel to it in the middle of the sheet, and Central Avenue curves across the bottom to Chestnut Street. The cross streets from Broad Avenue are Christie Heights, Harold Avenue, Hillside Avenue, Woodland Avenue (marked 'street not graded'), Beechwood Place, Magnolia Place and Elm Place, with Pine Terrace cutting diagonally from Magnolia Place to Central Avenue. North of Hillside Avenue the strip along the dividing line belongs to the Englewood Field Club golf course and golf grounds. The housing is detached frame dwellings, some stuccoed, a few with tile or brick veneer, on lots that are still largely vacant, especially in the narrow lots between Beechwood and Elm Places. Small shops and a dry cleaner stand on Hillside Avenue near Glenwood Avenue, and the public library stands at Broad and Central Avenues. East of Glenwood Avenue are Overlook Terrace, Hilltop Avenue and two cemeteries; further east two streets are marked 'street not open' and large blocks are empty. Highland Street and Pauline Boulevard reach Central Avenue at the bottom edge, and Irving Street is lettered in the corner. The heavy line in the upper right separates this part from part 2, which shows the block west of Broad Avenue. Margins refer to sheets 71, 72, 77 and 78.
notes: Renamed since: Central Av is now Fort Lee Road; Woodland Av is Woodland Place; Woodbridge Pl is Woodridge Place; Pauline Blvd is Paulin Boulevard; Christie Heights is Christie Heights Street.
Pine Terrace has no modern counterpart in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Two streets east of the cemetery are marked 'street not open'.
Public library at Broad Avenue and Central Avenue.
The modern Broad Avenue / Hillside Avenue junction (about 5 to 6 m off the drawn one) was excluded and Broad Avenue / Woodridge Place was rejected by the fit.

100 ft. Additional sheet Apr 1919 of the Palisades, N.J. volume; Leonia, not Cliffside Park. Turned about -29 degrees. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) Broad Av east to Glenwood Av and the cemeteries, Christie Heights to Central Av (now Fort Lee Road), with Harold, Hillside, Woodland (Woodland Pl), Beechwood, Magnolia, Elm, Pine Ter, Overlook Ter, Hilltop; part 2 (upper right, out of position) the block west of Broad between Grand Av, Christie Heights and Harrison St with Kingsley St and Leonia High School.

sheet-78-2.description: Second part of an additional sheet of April 1919 in Leonia, drawn at 100 ft to an inch in the upper right of the sheet above a heavy dividing line and at the same rotation as part 1, but placed out of position: it shows the block west of Broad Avenue, while part 1 shows the ground east of it. The part is bounded by Grand Avenue on the west, Christie Heights on the north, Broad Avenue on the east and Harrison Street on the south, with Kingsley Street running through the east end of the block. The dominant building is Leonia High School at the corner of Christie Heights and Broad Avenue, of brick with hollow-tile floors, an auditorium, manual training and domestic science rooms and a chemical laboratory, heated by steam and lit by electricity. North of Christie Heights the large lot 351 is otherwise empty. The block between Christie Heights and Harrison Street is divided into deep lots with detached frame dwellings, sheds, a poultry house and automobile garages. Short stubs of Leonia Avenue and Cooper Place leave the south side of Harrison Street at the dividing line. The town name Leonia is lettered across the top.
notes: The part is drawn out of position on the sheet: it lies west of Broad Avenue, to the left of part 1 on the ground.
Leonia High School at Christie Heights and Broad Avenue.
Cooper Pl corresponds to the modern Coover Street; Christie Heights is Christie Heights Street.
Grand Avenue is drawn only along the dividing line; its west side is not shown.
